title: Move money in one transaction
diff:
def transfer(conn, src, dst, cents):
    with conn:  # commits on success, rolls back on any exception
        row = conn.execute("SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = ?", (src,)).fetchone()
        if row[0] < cents:
            raise InsufficientFunds(src)
        conn.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?", (cents, src))
        conn.execute("UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?", (cents, dst))
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO ledger (src, dst, cents) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (src, dst, cents))

concepts.description: A transaction makes several statements succeed or fail together, so a crash cannot leave money debited but not credited.
concepts.context: the with conn block in transfers.py rolls back the debit if the credit or ledger insert raises

concepts.description: Reading a value and then acting on it is a race unless the read and the write are protected together, for example by a lock or a conditional update.
concepts.context: the balance SELECT before the UPDATE in transfers.py can see a stale balance if another transfer commits between them

concepts.description: Passing values as bound parameters keeps them out of the SQL text, which prevents injection.
concepts.context: every execute in transfers.py passes values as a tuple instead of formatting them into the query
